subject: Business Models
title: Groupon's Downfall
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Groupon's Downfall.

hook.text: Groupon was once the fastest-growing company ever. It turned down Google's $6 billion acquisition offer.

buildup.text: Daily deals attracted bargain hunters. Restaurants offered 50% off, hoping for repeat customers.

discovery.text: Deal-seekers rarely returned at full price. Merchants lost money on every deal and didn't gain loyal customers.

twist.text: Groupon's stock fell 95% from its IPO. The marketplace created value for nobody except short-term bargain hunters.

climax.text: Marketplaces must create sustainable value for both sides. One-sided value extraction always collapses.

punchline.text: Turned down $6 billion. Lost 95% of its value. Sustainable value matters.

quiz.question: Why did Groupon's marketplace model fail?
options: Deals attracted bargain hunters who never returned at full price

details.summary: Groupon built a daily deal marketplace that grew to the fastest IPO in history but collapsed because the marketplace served neither side well. Merchants lost money on deals without gaining repeat customers, and deal-seeking consumers had no loyalty to the platform or the businesses they visited.
details.whyItMatters: Groupon demonstrates that a marketplace where neither side achieves lasting value eventually collapses regardless of scale. Network effects only work when both sides benefit from participation..
takeaways: Merchants acquired deal-seekers who rarely returned at full price after the discount
Consumers were loyal to discounts, not to the platform or the merchants themselves
Fast growth masked the fundamental problem that neither marketplace side benefited long-term

faq.question: Why did Groupon's marketplace model fail structurally?
faq.answer: Merchants gave away 75 percent of revenue per deal customer. Those customers rarely returned at full price. The marketplace attracted price-sensitive consumers who were the least likely to become loyal..

faq.question: What would a sustainable local deal marketplace look like?
faq.answer: It would focus on customer retention rather than one-time discounts. Offer loyalty programs that reward repeat visits at full price. Help merchants build customer relationships through CRM tools. Charge lower margins that make merchant participation economically viable long-term.
